correctness.rationale: Grounding means taking the principal block, not deleting incident conductances; after normalization by b its clique and independent contrast eigenvalues are B=pt+q and p. The constant-on-type quotient has diagonal B-tx,p, off-diagonal entries -y,-x, and inverse trace (B-tx+p)/(p(B-tx)-xy). For the three follower counts the determinants are 2B, pt+p+q-1, 2p. When p=2 and CC there are only independent followers giving q/2, and when q=2 and UU there are only clique followers with eigenvalues B (multiplicity p-1) and 2. Both agree with the displayed formulas. The OU covariance is sigma^2/2 times the actual grounded inverse. For q=3, CC-UU has the sign of -(p-3)(pt-p+1). For p>=4 the UU-CU numerator is negative up through (p-1)/p by convexity and its equal negative endpoint values, and the CC-CU numerator is negative there with positive leading coefficient and one larger root. This checks all strict intervals and boundary ties. For p=3 the first difference vanishes identically and the decisive quadratic is 3t^2-2t-3. For p=2 the signs of 2t-1, t-1 and 2t^2-t-4 give the two stated transitions with the third type strictly worse at each. Expanding the larger-root discriminant as p^2((p^2-3p)^2+64p-32) gives the stated asymptotic. Pair counts follow from the orbits. Inspected verify.py without executing it: 420 direct inverse comparisons and four symbolic comparisons are finite corroboration; the printed 17 threshold checks refer to 17 p values with several sign checks per value, not 17 universal identities.

value.rationale: Three evaluable costs replace the pair search, but the main value is the exact coupling-driven movement of optimal leader types in a small peripheral class. The p=3 persistent degeneracy and the reversal in phase order from p=2 to p>=4 reveal how clique reinforcement competes with grounding the periphery; a single unit-weight classification does not reveal these regimes.
